General Talic himself is talking about difficulties in expulsion or expelling because of transportation problems and because the residents themselves are resisting leaving their areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Following on from that in part 3, General Talic talks about the transformation of the JNA into the SR BiH and the changes of names, measures aimed at strengthening the organisational structure of the army, the unification of command structure system, overall structures, establishment of new units. In essence, this is the formation and transformation of the JNA into the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we look at page 4, there is a -- at the bottom of the page, a comment about the problem of looting, which is occurring. "Negligent conduct by members of the TO and individual groups of volunteers is the main reason behind the looting and destruction of property. Even though the majority of soldiers are annoyed with such conduct, it would be difficult to stop the looting without imposing the most severe forms of punishment."

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, General Talic makes reference to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So that's a clear recognition of this problem and a concern that it would be difficult to stop without really -- what is the concern do you think with imposing the most severe forms of punishment in order to stop a problem like this?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Well, I can only really go on what is stated in the document. General Talic is clearly aware of the issue and is saying it's difficult to stop it without imposing this severe restriction and therefore that would assume that severe restrictions would be needed to curb this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then he in fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, was he facing another problem at the time that of -- namely that of desertion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was. There was significant references to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And according to your judgement, having seen per used several of these documents, would imposing these restrictions and proceedings for looting have helped the army? Or more or less would have been interpreted as unacceptable by the soldiers and the rest of the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Are you asking me, Your Honour, from a perspective of my own military background or from the documentation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, from the perspective of what you have read. In other words, why does General Talic write that "proceeding or prosecuting for looting would be problematic"? Would it be something that would be popular amongst the troops or would it be something that was logistically impossible at the time? Why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there were difficulties at this specific time in relation to the establishments of military courts, although other documentation notes that they were up and running in August 1992. I'm not sure I can specifically answer your question in relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: My question is a very simple one. Usually I would expect to find a document referring to this specific problem of looting stating, gentlemen, there is -- we have a problem, that's looting in general, but I as a general have tackled the bull from the horns and I'm taking all necessary actions to curtail on this practice and will report back later on. Why doesn't General Talic say this and instead he writes what he -- what you read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can only -- in relation to the issue of looting, General Talic did write a number of instructions through 1992 and highlighted that as a problem. I can explain maybe later why he gave justification as to why it was a problem. People were having to leave the front line and it was causing difficulties with him. It seemed that General Talic -- he did state in some documents that he was holding commanders responsible for taking action to curb this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have seen those documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But it appears there was not -- from my perspective and from the documents I have reviewed, this robust -- robust measures that he articulated here were taken to stamp out the problem, irrespective of whether they were going to be acceptable to the lower soldiers who may have been conducting that activity or whether for any other reason. As far as I can I think, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's enough for me, thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just for completeness, under part 5 on this document requests -- General Talic does request that more stringent measures against looters be introduced. However, if I understood you and I think you explained it later in your report, looting remained a problem throughout the period of 1992.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. It was there are a number of references, as we have talked about, and I covered it in the report that General Talic I believe was genuinely unhappy with individual instances of looting and I think he saw it as a disciplinary issue as well as an operational one. It was causing him problems with soldiers having to leave the front line because they themselves -- he certainly saw when the looting affected Serbian houses or Serbian areas that it was causing a problem too. He does put a request in here, it's a request not an order, which is unusual, but he does say: Introduce more stringent measures. He didn't say what they should be. He doesn't say report back. And interestingly he limits himself to the issue of looting, war profiteering, and speculation, as opposed to some extent the most obvious problem which would seem to be the expulsion of a large number of people who are from those areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. We've already started talking about the emphasis placed, which you can see on these documents, on cooperation and coordination with civilian bodies and that is a section of your report which we will cover. The next document deals with that in some respects as well as the military goals which are being put forward in this period. That's footnote 82. It's dated 14 September, 1992, command of the 1st Krajina Corps report on military consultations, and I will need to enter this as an exhibit. It doesn't yet have an exhibit number. That will be P2418. If we take a look at this document, it talks about in the first paragraph: "The main objective of the consultations was to achieve maximum unit and resolve. Important problems in the ongoing effort of the Serbian people to create a new state." And can you just comment a bit about this meeting and why you selected this document as an illustration?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. This document was with a number of senior and significant military figures from the VRS, Minister of National Defence, and the co-commander and 26 -- presidents of 26 municipalities and police representatives in September. And it appeared to me, being a very important meeting in essence trying to iron out whatever difficulties they felt they had but also articulating their achievements to date and articulated, as you say -- the main objective was to achieve unity which was an issue which was regularly talked about, resolve important problems with the aim of creating their own new Serbian state, which was in essence what the 16th assembly session articulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think if you look at page 5, point 1, the point is made again: "The following conclusions were reached, one ensure complete unity in the further struggle of the Serbian people to create their own state."

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are there any other areas of this document you'd like to comment on before we move on?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I think part 3 is of interest in terms of again this unity and cooperation issue. "The functioning of the authorities is a significant element of the struggle and the resistance of the army of the Serbian republic. Because of this, it is necessary to support the legal organs of authorities until they are elected and enable them to do the best in performing their duties" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you slow down, please, when you read documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This cuts again to this issue in the report that I discuss coordination and cooperation with the -- between the military, and it was as important for the military to assist the authorities in the performance of their duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like us to now look at the next document cited in footnote 83 to your report. That is P380. A 1st of June, 1992, 1st Krajina Corps command report, again on the current political and security situation. This is also authored by Colonel Vukelic.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. Again I flag this document up for a couple of areas. One is returning to this issue of resettlement and the movement out -- of personnel from the area. In the third paragraph: "A portion of the Muslim and Croatian population is moving out. The region of Bosnian Krajina has issued a decision to facilitate such departures, providing that the Serbs from central Bosnia and places with predominantly Muslim and Croatian populations are also allowed to move out. Those departing will not be allowed to return." I would argue this again reflects back on this issue of resettlement. A little bit further on in this report, on the page -- page 2, there is a very brief reference to 100 families in Novo Gradiska -- wrong, I'm sorry, it's -- in Kotor Varos, been requesting to move to Novo Gradiska. On page 3 I would draw your attention to the top line: "The municipalities of Bosanska Gradiska, Srbac, Laktasi, and Prnjavor are stable and Muslims and Croatian extremists have started handing in their weapons." This is an issue which I will talk later on in the report. Again there is a comment that this report should be thrashed out with all soldiers, specifying that the facts present are more credible than those in the mass media. Again highlighting that this issue of departures, expulsions, moving out, resettlement was being disseminated down through the military chain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that again is part of explaining to the soldiers on the ground what the conflict is about, what they are fighting for; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we look at the document you cite in footnote 84, this is a command of the 30th Partisan division report from 19 July, 1992, this is Exhibit P1738, you refer to this report again talking about the relationship between the VRS and the civilian governmental authorities. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. This is a slightly lower level than the Krajina Corps. It's again back to the 30th division and it's -- they themselves are passing down or reporting about the political and security situation. And if I draw your attention to page 2: "The general military and political situation, the opening of the Posavina corridor and the successful establishment and functioning of links with Yugoslavia" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Slow down when you're reading the document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The opening of the Posavina corridor and the successful establishment and functioning of links with Yugoslavia are considerable achievements by the army of SR BH." This again cuts to strategic goal number 2. "Prijedor region units firmly control their zone where they are mopping up in the remaining Muslim extremists." And part B in relation to the 30th division: "So far, the 30th Partisan division has conducted combat operations in the territory of the municipalities of Kljuc, Mrkonjic Grad, Sipovo, Kupres, Donji Vakuf, Jajce, Bugojno, Travnik, Skender Vakuf, as far as Kotor Varos and Teslic." And it states: "By conducting combat operations in this area, our division has made possible the establishment and functioning of the government in the Serbian Republic of BH, organs of government have already been established and function in Donji Vakuf, Kupres, Kljuc, Sipovo, Skender Vakuf, and Kotor Varos, while in Jajce they have been established and function in the part of the municipality liberated and held by the forces of our division." On page 3, there are a number of sections of interest. The fourth paragraph states: "We have established cooperation with the relevant bodies of government in the SR BiH on the territory taken by the 30th Partisan division." Does make --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, again, can you link that up with the earlier order we talked about, that was part of the mobilisation order, was it not, that these links should be established as soon as possible?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. I'm sorry, please continue.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: There are other references in this section which talk about cooperating with the local populations in the zone of responsibility of the division. I draw your attention to the section that starts: "A special problem in the zone of responsibility is posed by Muslims and Croats who are seeking permission to move out of the area in which they live and move to territories held by the forces of the green berets and Croatian Defence Council. Permission has thus been sought for the relocation of 110 Muslims from Donji Vakuf to Bugojno. The Red Cross in Mrkonjic Grad is negotiating with the HVO from Jajce about exchanging civilians. Serbs from Jajce for Croats and Muslims from Mrkonjic Grad, Jajce and Sipovo on the principle of allowing people to choose freely where they want to live, where they will live. This exchange is effective -- affected successfully -- sorry, if this exchange is affected successfully, it will be followed by an exchange of prisoners of war." Again cutting to this whole issue of resettling and moving people. On page 4, I just draw your attention to the top paragraph: "The army of the SR BH will continue to implement resolutely and uncompromisingly the decisions of the state and political leadership of the SR BH. It is essential to liberate and keep a firm hold on the territories of the SR BH." I draw your attention to what Dr. Kalinic had said in the 16th assembly in terms of controlling territory. And the section that reads: "The commands and units will provide the greatest possible assistance to the local organs of government in consolidating the situation on the ground, reviving economic and social functions, and preventing lawlessness and wilful behaviour."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to be clear, that's a typo, isn't it, in the English version of this document?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's signed by Stanislav Galic. I'd also like to look briefly at the document you cite in footnote 85 of your report. This is from April 1993, I believe. It's a main staff report concerning combat readiness in 1992. So this is a report looking back --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you intend to tender this evidence, Mr. Nicholls, because it's not according to my information at least?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour. It has not yet been made an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this will be P2419?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's correct, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, is this an excerpt from a larger document?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It's a very large document, Your Honour, and this is only a small section of it which I put in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I think there are three sections here which are of relevance. Why did you pick this and put this one in? What is the most important part of this document?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was a document written by the main staff in April 1993 entitled: "Analysis of Combat Readiness." And in essence it was a reflection back into 1992 and looking at the activities of the VRS in that year and highlighting problems and difficulties and suggesting solutions to those, in a similar way to the JNA document we discussed at footnote 1 this morning. In this document, there are a number of sections that relate to the development of the main staff and the functioning of the army and I highlight a couple of those sections here. In the section that starts: "In the past year, 1992, from self-organised units at the local level, the army of the Republika Srpska has grown into the highest strategic organisational formation of the Serbian people in former BH, capable of realising the strategic and other objectives assigned to it by the Supreme Command and the president of the Republika Srpska as the Supreme Commander. At the same time, the main staff of the army of the Republika Srpska, together with its army, by relying on the Serbian people, the Serbian Orthodox Church, and the SDS has grown into a strategic level high command and equipped itself to control and command operational, tactical, and other formations in the armed struggle and war in general." And if I draw your attention to the next paragraph: "The swift development of the army of the Republika Srpska and of its organisation and capability to conduct combat operations in a religious, ethnic, and civil war was achieved primarily thanks to the quick self organising and adjustment of remnants of the TO to the local conditions of struggle and the protection of the Serbian people. It was achieved thanks to the guidance of the SDS, which after its electoral victory led the Serbian people in a just struggle against the Muslim Croat forces. These initial forms and conserval successes in the initial period of the war were accepted by the commands of the tactical and operational units and by the main staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, as well as by decent patriotically orientated officers of the former JNA who placed the interests of the Serbian people above and considered them more important than ideology, more important than their families and personal property. And even though the number of active officers in the units of the army of the Republika Srpska grew only slowly, in our assessment together with the reserve commanding officer and fighting men played a decisive role in the development, strengthening growth and battle hardening of the army of the RS."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm not sure with this excerpt if I have that right available to me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next section on page 159 of the translation in the second paragraph states: "The strategic objectives of our war which were promptly defined and set before the main staff of the army of the RS, the commands and units served as a general guideline upon which we planned the actual operations and concerted battles. That means objectives were set before us, rather than specific tasks spelled out. Although the President of the republic as the Supreme Commander of the armed forces of the RS did orally assign a number of tasks which were of general and vital significance to the -- our struggle and protecting the Serbian people and its territories." This I would argue makes specific reference to strategic goals as being a bedrock, if you like, of military action, certainly after -- for the main staff's perspective and the VRS from the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And again, you cited this as an example of the primacy of the role of the political leadership over the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are moving too slowly, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll try to speed us along, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Let's move to the document you cite in footnote 89. This is a 20th of August command of the 1 KK corps document. This is not an exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This will be 2420.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you, Mr. Brown?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, essentially, you've cited this report again as an example of documentation you have found in the military records which reflect the goals set forth at the -- and the objectives set forth in the 16th assembly; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. In my report I argue that the ultimate aim, if you like, was to unify the Serb lands which was hinted at in Karadzic's speech of the 12th assembly. But if you go to paragraph 2 of this report states that: "There are some problems but -- and that those problems are potentially putting the Serbian peoples fight at risk and that the objective is clear, the objective is to liberate all Serbian people who live in Bosnia-Herzegovina and then unite them with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and other Serbian peoples on the territory of the former Yugoslavia." And I've dedicated a small section of the report to that, my belief that that was the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just for the record, you said Karadzic speech in the 12th assembly, you meant the 16th assembly, no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to move -- this is a related topic but it's a little bit different going back in time now to April of 1992. When you came back from the break, you stated that you wanted to make it clear that this -- important military operations had been in place before the 16th assembly session. If we look at the document you cite in footnote 116, which appears now -- we are now on page 37 on your report, I'd like to ask you some questions about that document and about earlier mobilisations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This you're tendering in evidence and it will be P2421, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead and Ms. Chuqing will deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe why you included this section of your report which describes mobilisation which took place on the territory earlier than the May mobilisation order signed by General Talic which we covered a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: The issue of mobilisation had been of importance for the Bosnian Serb authorities or the SDS prior to the announcements in May and this document I believe is important because in April there still was some concern about the future status of the JNA and whether it was going to be staying in Bosnia, whether it was going to be leaving, and this decision to mobilise the Serbian TO on the 15th and 16th of April I thought was of significance because it's the -- an early indication that an armed force was being mobilised for operations before the establishment of the VRS as a recognised army or an army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now this document we are looking at is a decision as you say stating that: "A state of imminent threat of war is hereby declared." And 2: "The mobilisation of the TO, the Territorial Defence, that is, in the whole territory of Serbian BH is hereby ordered," and it's signed by Drs. Plavsic and Koljevic. Can we talk about the next document, P117, in relation to this order dated the 16th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is P153, Your Honours. It's already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe this document to be of some significance and follows on from the previous one. It is in essence an expansion of that instruction by and written or signed or signature block anyway by Bogdan Subotic who was the Minister of Defence. It takes those decisions to declare an imminent threat of war and mobilisation and expands them, and according to the distribution was to be sent to the governments of the autonomous regions and the SAOs and to Serbian municipalities. I draw your attention to point 1: "The Territorial Defence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina shall be established as an armed force of the SR BiH. Command and control of Territorial Defence will be exercised, municipal, district, and regional staffs and the republican staff of the S BiH TO." In the explanation, there are a couple of sections I think are particularly important. Part 2, set up district staffs in districts. "This matter is hereby placed under the jurisdiction of the governments of the SAOs, organise the staffs on the same principle of the formation and the former zone staffs. And this above also applies to the autonomous region Bosanska Krajina." By that I believe he's saying establish some TO or Defence staff at those levels, but point 3 I think is of -- significance. "The declaration of an imminent threat of war shall entail the taking of all necessary measures appropriate to the situation and in accordance with the specific situation in a given territory." I believe Subotic is giving those the document is directed significant leeway to take all necessary measures in essence in relation to an imminent threat of war, mobilisation, and the likes. And the last section: "In the preparations for training and deployment of TO units, affect cooperation with the JNA units and where possible establish unified command."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So then this order is giving authority as you say to the different districts to respond as they see fit and necessary depending on changing circumstances in different areas, to the imminent threat of war?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: After the establishment of the VRS, into May through June, would these units have become integrated into the VRS?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. That was specifically instructed at the 16th assembly session on the 12th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So, correct me if I'm wrong, this is essentially an emergency mobilisation to create fighting forces all across the territory, including the AR Krajina in order to respond or carry out military options until the VRS is formally established, until there is a more formal Serb army?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And finally, I think this can be related back to the VRS main staff report from April 1993 that we talked about earlier, which was footnoted in footnote 85 which talked about the growth of the army from localised TO units into a more organised centralised structure, is that --

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Is there anything else you wish to say about this document?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: No, not at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm going to try to turn now to another section of your report which begins on page 44. You've done a section of your report on -- entitled: "Cooperation with Civilian Bodies." And we've already seen through some of the documents we've looked at that there was a general feature of when units were established or were sent to different regions that they were to immediately make contact and cooperate with the local civilian authorities. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I think we've highlighted some of those already.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If you can -- I think it's pretty self-evident but this is a fairly substantial section of the report. Could you just give us a very brief overview of why, when you were preparing this report, you decided that you needed to put in a section on this topic?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I believe that it was a significant feature and component was referenced significantly in the documentation that I reviewed and merited some analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you talk in -- I just want to clear this up -- in paragraph 1.03, about a coordinating function that was the primary role of Serb Crisis Staffs and civilian bodies. Can you just tell us what you mean. What is your definition of a coordinating function?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Coordination I would argue brings together or synchronises components or groups with a common purpose or a common task, in order to complete, fulfil a common task.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look first at the document you cite as in footnote 151. This is an excerpt from the instructions for the work of the municipal Crisis Staffs of the Serbian people. This is P157. This goes to what we were just talking about in this section of your report. Could you tell us why you included this in I think the first points 2 and 3 are of most relevance?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. These instructions to me indicate that this Crisis Staff is a coordinating body, each of whom has its own competencies or responsibilities and it coordinates the function of authority in order to defends territories. And it makes reference to some of the component parts to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you speak in your report in paragraph 1.103 some of the component parts, some of the functioning was to bring together the relevant civilian, military, and police bodies in a formalised grouping. That's what we are talking about here. Correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. And this instruction amongst others I would argue does that or states that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to look at a document you cite in footnote 154. That appears on page 46 of your report and this is Exhibit 1010, Your Honours. It's a report on the work of the Crisis Staff or War Presidency of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly in the period since 15th of May, 1992, and it's dated; Kljuc July, 1992. We don't need to go through this entire document but I think you have selected this as an example of the proposition that municipal Crisis Staffs served this coordinating function. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. I think on page 3 it articulates that: "During the armed conflicts, representatives (commanders of the army of Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina) regularly attended the Crisis Staff and War Presidency meetings. They commanded and carried out the war activities for the defence of the territory and citizens of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly against Muslim extremists. They cooperated and coordinated everything very well with the Crisis Staff of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly." And I would argue that that would seem to echo very much the Branko Djeric instruction in April about this coordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And it also echoes, does it not, the -- very similar to the efforts we saw in P51, that's the document that was cited in footnote 77 of your report, which is the meeting attended by presidents of the municipalities in areas within the 30th Division's region or area of control in which the 16th assembly session conclusions were spoken of and there was talk about regular meetings every two weeks in order to coordinate the implementation of those goals?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, as well as the Galic instruction of, I believe, the 19th of July where he himself is making reference to the fact that they had this relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Similarly, I think we can go through this fairly quickly, if we look at the next document, this is footnoted in footnote 158. This is P686, Your Honours. And it's a Sanski Most -- Serbian Municipality of Sanski Most Crisis Staff set of conclusions dated the 30th of May, 1992. The beginning of this document states that, "for better and more effective work by the Crisis Staff, several points were agreed. A: The Crisis Staff consists of the following 12 persons, each having a clear domain of activities." The first person being Nedeljko Rasula who was the President of the Crisis Staff and it goes on the Court is familiar with these names but we can see here representatives of the police, Mirko Vrucinic, of the Serbian Territorial Defence command, the commander in that case, Nedjo Anicic and the 6th Krajina Brigade commander, Branko Basara?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I think this is a very clear example of the Djeric instruction in activities of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if we look at page 2 and we see some of the topics which are being discussed at this meeting, making a list of refugees from Mahala detained in the sports hall and the school centre who are fit for military service, making lists of people who are currently located in the public security station, and then a tasking in point 4. Are these typical examples of the types of things where these different representatives from the military civilian police would be present and would discuss in the documents you've looked through?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. In many of them and again these points, if you like, a generic phrase, could be termed defence issues or control issues of the territory, and I would argue that again cuts to the instructions about the Crisis Staff's role.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We've come across tens and tens and tens of similar documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour. I just think that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think you need to stress this much through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: What I'm trying to show, Your Honour, is that through somebody who has studied the military documents, studied the military operations, put together a report on the relevant military developments from that perspective in the Krajina in 1992, that this is an important part of the report looking at it from a purely military perspective as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, just -- excuse me, Your Honours. In paragraph 1.111 on page 48, you go through some of the many areas in which Crisis Staffs, municipal Crisis Staffs or War Presidencies made decisions?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. I list in that section some of the, again, if you like, the defence or related tasks that I saw from the documents I was able to look at or reviewed and listed some of those in relation to Crisis Staffs, so establishing new light brigades, financing issues, mobilisation issues, I think they listed -- they are listed here and footnoted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could just look at the document, as an example you cite in footnote 168, that is P921, Your Honours, it is a Kljuc municipality Crisis Staff order from a meeting held on the 28th of May, 1992. Very briefly, can you tell us why you selected this document as one of the examples of the military issues which the Crisis Staffs addressed?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: This one in particular made reference to the issue of weapon deadlines and that vigorous measures would be implemented to carry out a disarmament which would have disastrous consequences as it's stated here for the security of both people and property. It also makes mention in paragraph 6 to a defence-related issue in terms of armed forces and White Eagles are to put themselves under the command of the 30th Division, so it flags up again if you like defence or military-related issues in a Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Brown, you are aware that for some time at least there was or it is suggested that there was the Autonomous Region of Krajina, which also had its Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you aware of any documents emanating from the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina more or less along the same lines that you have identified in these documents coming out of the municipal Crisis Staffs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff involving matters relating to the military.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I think later on I would like to introduce some documents that cut to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Shall we move to those? Because I think they are more important for the purpose of this trial than the municipal Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if it's possible to have a short bathroom break? I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Brown, it happens to me and to everyone else in this room. We can wait for you, if it's okay with you, or we can go out as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's skip ahead, Mr. Brown, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Only skipping one page.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to talk about the event you talk about and relate in paragraph 1.114 of the your report. That's on page 50. You found it relevant and significant to enter that ARK Crisis Staff members - and I take it there you mean the regional Crisis Staff - also toured the areas of combat activity and were briefed by military personnel in order to gain an understanding of the situation. And then you talk about footage and a transcript which we have got of Mr. Brdjanin where he tours Kotor Varos as an example of what you're talking about in that paragraph, footnote 188.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The transcript of that brief section we are going to look at is P1598.1. We are not going to play the tape, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The Court has already directed to you this topic. Can you just tell us why you included this and what the significance is of this section where Mr. Brdjanin is describing what parts of his role as president of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I felt it was a reasonably significant section from the video. "Let me tell you that being president of the autonomous region Crisis Staff it is my responsibility to tour all the front lines. I have to admit that I most frequently toured the corridor, the passage to Serbia, Simply, today's visit, the reason for this visit is that every Monday I must inform the presidents of all Crisis Staffs about the political situation in the region. We should clear our area, which definitely encompasses Kotor Varos and Jajce, and the most important battle being waged is the one I toured yesterday, the breakthrough to Serbia. We can see for ourselves that there is simply no point in further negotiations with those we are at war with or who are at war with us. Those who took up arms must be defeated, must surrender their weapons and total Serbian rule must be established here." There are a couple of issues. The issue of touring the front line or touring the territory is important. Informing others about what he has seen in the front line and combat areas, the referencing to "clear the territory," the issue of the importance of the corridor, cutting again to the 16th assembly session, the reference to weapon deadlines which I would argue is a very important issue in relation to military operations in May and June, and also the reference to total Serbian rule being established. So for those bullet points, even though it's a very short section, I think it's relatively revealing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Then again, although we have been talking somewhat in detail about the municipal Crisis Staffs, would you agree this is a sort of mirrored function at the ARK level? The importance of being aware of coordinating with the military operations in the area?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, and what would bear that out possibly even more is the fact that the rest of the video includes significant military and police figures in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And maybe just before we move on if you'd like to -- who are you referring to by that? We can take a look at the document.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel Bosko Pelic was a subordinate commander of General Talic. He was an operational group commander in the Vlasic area, which covered Kotor Varos and he controlled the brigades in those areas. Stojan Zupljanin, of course, chief of the Banja Luka CSB and other CSB, special police detachment, figures I believe are on that video, so in the context it's not only what Mr. Brdjanin says, but it's also the figures who are there at the same time. And that video is shot in Kotor Varos in a -- at a point in time, I believe, when there is a -- to use their phrase crisis. It's -- action is occurring there, and the fact that these figures are there for me is as revealing as what is said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. In footnote 92 -- 192, excuse me, you cite the conclusions of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina from the 22nd of May, 1992. And I think it's good for us to look at this briefly because as you say in your report, although there was a relationship and coordinating function of the Crisis Staffs and close coordination between the military and the civilian bodies, I think to use your words, it was not always a seamless relationship, and can you just tell us why you included this document, which, in essence, is a complaint about the attendance of General Talic at Crisis Staff meetings in point 4?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I do state, I believe, in the report that the relationship was not always seamless, that there were difficulties and problems highlighted in the military documentation. I included a reference earlier on that complaints that the ARK, were encroaching on military related issues, there are one or two complaints from General Talic through 1992 of that. The operations of municipal Crisis Staffs did to some degree vary. Some stages the military commander appeared to be a member of the Crisis Staff; Sanski Most document we have looked at. In other ones, they were if you like an ex officio member who would come in and brief on the political security situation. So there was not always a seamless relationship and I would argue from the documentation I've seen that there always was, and this is an example on the 22nd of May if it's to be taken at face value, that there are complaining that there is poor coordination between the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the army and that General Talic is to attend or a person designated by him. And from other documentation, it appears that staff officers from General Talic's corps did attend the Crisis Staff, so this is, for me, just an example to highlight that this relationship was not always a seamless one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we jump to page 53 of your report, paragraph 1.122, you state that despite these difficulties, and they were some of the problems you've been talking about now and strains on the military civilian relationship highlighted above, there were attempts to rectify these problems. Meetings were held with regional and municipal authority leaders and this included attempts to stop what the military saw as undue interference in its professional work. And then in footnote 206, you cite an example of what the military saw as potential interference in its work. I'd like just to look at that document. This is a 1st Krajina Corps command regular combat report dated the 2nd of August, 1992. Your Honours, this is P403, we have seen it before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I think the relevant section, Mr. Brown, is section 5 on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think it's also P1447.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This may be one -- I saw that it may have another exhibit number, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And can you just briefly describe what this says to you. There has been a meeting and the 1KK seems to be feeling optimistic that, as it says, attempts by the Autonomous Region of Krajina authorities will not to interfere or involve themselves in matters of military organisation will not happen again. I may not have paraphrased that perfectly but could you tell us why you included this section?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Well, for the reasons we've been discussing, that clearly there has been some highlighted difficulties between the military's perspective, the Autonomous Region of Krajina authorities and the Serbian republic government and that if this isn't dealt with, that it might have some problems for the military. But in order to rectify that, there has been a meeting at which promises have been made that the autonomous region will not, in essence, place themselves above the military and that they believe the meeting has been a very constructive one. So I wanted to highlight that again to show that the relationship was not always seamless but there were mechanisms in order to -- in place in order to try and resolve those difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to turn now to a topic which has been discussed in this case but I'd be interested in hearing your perspective on it, and that is the dismissal of Muslim and Croat officers from the VRS. The relevant pages in your report are pages 55 through 59, I think. You stated in your executive summary that Muslim and Croat officers in positions of authority were removed from the VRS in June, 1992. This process of removal involved the RK government, the VRS main staff and the 1st Krajina Corps. I'd like to just quickly go through that chain of events. First of all, you include --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour? I think maybe this is one of those areas that you suggested that I speak of. I really don't have any contest that Muslim and Croat officers left the JNA, in some cases were removed from the JNA. I mean there was a war going on between the Serbs and the Muslims and Croats on the other side. It makes no sense if you're engaged in a war that you maintain an officer corps composed of representatives of the other side of the conflict. So I don't even know why this is an issue. I don't know why the Prosecution is making a big issue out of it. It's the sensible thing to do. Serbs were dismissed from the Bosnian forces, I assume. I know one Serb served as a general in the Bosnian forces but I mean, there was people fighting each other here and this just make any sense to me, but I don't contest it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Point taken, Mr. Ackerman but in this part of the expert witness's report, the role played by your client is highlighted, and perhaps the questions can be limited to Mr. Brdjanin's role as described and commented upon by the witness. The rest, I think we take it that persons like Colonel Hasotic and others were indeed removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'll try to go through it quickly but he has put it in his report and I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This came up already on previous occasions and if in a few words, I think the comment made by Mr. Ackerman needs to be taken into consideration because if I am fighting you, I wouldn't ask your brothers and sisters to come and help me against you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, that seems to me an argument he can make at the appropriate time. It's not really an objection, as I hear it and he's certainly not stipulating, I don't think, to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's stick to Radoslav Brdjanin here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I do recall that we spent an awful lot of time on this when another former officer testified here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Keep it short. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: First of all, Mr. Brown, just to be clear, as Mr. Ackerman has stated, there was a problem with people of different ethnicities fighting in this type of war on -- in the same armies. If we look very quickly at -- before we get into June, at footnote 235. This has not been exhibited, I don't believe. It's a 1st Krajina command report 31st of May, 1992, a regular combat report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, 235, you said, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I'm sorry, that's on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 57.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And this will be P2?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's go right to point 5. "State of security and morale." We see there that one of the problems which is being discussed under state of morale is that "some conscripts of Muslim nationality have asked to be released from their units -- from the units." They express their dissatisfaction with the massive destruction of their towns. Skipping ahead a sentence, "this is made worse by public statements made in the media by the SDS, Serbian Democratic Party, Bosanska Krajina autonomous region leaders who advocate moving and expelling all Muslims and Croats from these areas." Now, very briefly, you've included this because it shows that there is a problem with the units with different nationalities, the Muslims and Croats are unhappy with what they see going on and military actions by the VRS and that's made worse by the statements of the Autonomous Region of Krajina leadership in the media; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I think there is a -- that summarises it. There are a couple of other smaller issues. The fact that Muslims and Croats who responded to the mobilisation and conscripts of Serbian nationality who had previously avoided military obligations are accepted into units with reluctance, has a most disadvantageous influence on the morale of troops. So clearly there are certain Muslims who had responded to the mobilisation and are -- and were in the VRS - that's one area - but your points are right. It makes clear that conscripts of Muslim nationality have been asked to leave because they are dissatisfied with what had had happened in their towns and that the leadership of the SDS and the Krajina had also been advocating moving out and expelling Muslims and Croats from these areas, so I think it's it speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now we won't go through it but this is not a document cited in your report, just to lay the chronology, I'm referring to P229, Your Honours, that is the document of 7th of June, 1992, headed in Sanski Most.
