utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will have a 25 minute break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In the absence of Ms. Gustin --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We started -- we are going it try to quickly go through the section of your report which you entitled: "Removal of Muslims and Croats From the Military." One document which is not in your report, it's been exhibited as P229, is a 7th of June Sanski Most conclusion adopted at a subregional meeting and we began to talk about that before the break. Do you remember this document we are discussing?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Are you aware of this document, although it's not footnoted in your report?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Item 4 of this set of demands sent to the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Banja Luka is the demand that the 1st Krajina Corps in Banja Luka and particularly General Momir Talic of the 1st Krajina Corps, purge the 1st Krajina Corps of Muslims and Croats. And it goes on to state that the rationale is that they are not reliable fighters against their own people. And later on, a deadline is set for that of seven days. And on paragraph 6 of that same document, there is sort of a threat that if action is not taken, the seven municipalities will take the Muslims and Croats of their municipalities under escort, military escort, to the centre of Banja Luka. Now, there is a reaction to this on the 9th of June by the 1st Krajina Corps, and that's a document you footnote as 221.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that's P1582, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. This document headed Command of the 1st Krajina Corps, 9th of June, 1992, report on the Autonomous Region of Krajina staff decision states that one of the issues that was discussed at yesterday's session of the autonomous region Bosnian Krajina Crisis Staff was a general personnel policy in the army of the 1st Krajina Corps. Now, just to begin with, that's another example of the type of communication and coordination that we have been discussing, that there was a briefing to the army of what's being done in the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Well, clearly the army were aware or were made aware of the discussions that the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff the previous day, and that's been briefed into the military chain.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And the document continues, that: "An ultimatum was issued requesting removal of these persons, it speaks of 67 officers of Muslim or Croatian nationality by June 15th, 1992, or they will take over control of the armed forces." And the document continues that: "The role of the 1st Krajina Corps is that these demands are justified but there will be problems enacting replacements within the deadline of 15th June." Can you just comments briefly on this section, in particular about this threat to take over control of the armed forces which you note in your report.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Well, to some extent I think it may speak for itself but they clearly view this issue of some significance and feel that if it isn't actioned that they are -- should be in a position to take control over the army because presumably it would therefore not be following an objective that they believed was of importance. It's also of note that they seem to have fairly reasonable knowledge of the numbers of Muslims and Croats in the Krajina Corps logistic base and air defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we skip ahead to your footnote 225.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's the 13th of June, 1992 1st Krajina Corps command report. It's P383, Your Honours, just highlight in point 6 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, footnote what?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's on page 57 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just -- I take it you have included this document to show that in fact that process began. In point 6 we see the statement that: "The purging of officers on an ethnic basis remains a topic of discussion because of the danger that it may very soon result in deficiencies in the units but it's proceeding in the spirit of the order received."

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. And that is referring to the Mladic order which occurred as a result of the Vukelic instruction which we just read out on the 9th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think we need it go through that order. You've cited it in your report. Footnote 228 is a June 22nd, 1992, decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That is P254, Your Honours, with a different ERN number. I'm sorry, the ERN number cited in the report does not match exactly the ERN of the previous exhibit for the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you've cited this report for the proposition of showing, I take it, that this process of removing persons of non-Serb ethnicity from important posts had taken place in the army as well as in other important spheres of the political and military society?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. I believe you can't necessarily separate out what was happening in the military from what was happening elsewhere. The issue of Serbs in positions of authority in the police had already been discussed and there was an issue in April, and as was issues of other executive management posts and the like. And I see what happened in the military as something that was already occurring in other areas, and in relation specifically to the Autonomous Region of Krajina, it's clear that they had an involvement in this process, and the removal of non-Serbs from positions of authority was within the military is in its nature a military or defence-related issue. And I think from -- from that small sequence of documents, it's clear that municipal, regional, and military organs were involved in that process. They came to a decision that Muslims and Croats should be removed, they were removed, and the military implemented that decision, that the initial -- the initial impetus appeared to have come from municipal and regional -- regional level decisions and it was -- it was actioned by the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And again, just going back, this was something, this topic was something which had been raised by Mr. Brdjanin at the 16th assembly session. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, it had.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In fact, we also talk a little -- talked a little bit about General Mladic's position at that time which appears to have changed by June of 1992. He is now agreeing with this expulsion or separation of non-Serbs from the military?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, he is. His instruction of the 9th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. The next section of your report I'd like to talk about is what is -- is within the section of military operations in your report. You spoke in your executive summary of how many of the municipality-level operations contained common features which included the movement of forces into and surrounding of non-Serb areas prior to combat activities, the issuance of deadlines and the shelling and attacking of villages, cooperation with TO and police units, the forcible movement of sections of the population for questioning into detention camps, killings, looting, and movement of many of the non-Serbs from the area. What I want to talk about now to begin with is one of the common features which you discuss in that summary section, which is the issuance of deadlines. I take it when you say "deadlines" in that summary you're talking about the deadlines for the surrender of weapons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. The phrase they often use is the surrender of illegal-held weapons or weapons held by paramilitary units. Those are the deadlines I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is the issue of disarmament?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This section begins on page 64 of your report, paragraph 2.10, and again just let me emphasise this and make sure it's correct, you said that many of the combat operations especially those in May and early June of 1992 were justified as operations to disarm paramilitary groups and often initially involved the issuance of an ultimatum or deadline to hand over illegally held weapons.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. Those often are the phrases used in military documents at the time, especially in May and June. It wasn't the only justification I hasten to add that military documents give for their combat operations. They often regularly used phrases such as to control territory or mop up operations. But many of the combat operations that I see referenced in the military documents do give this justification that they are disarming paramilitary groups and do reference the issue of weapon deadlines.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. The first document I'd like to look at in connection with this topic is footnoted as footnote 261.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is P167, Your Honours. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it also P1182?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll have to ask Ms. Gustin. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could you -- do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Could you please explain -- this is early in May, 4th of May, 1992, the relevance why you included this decision of the Ministry of National Defence of the Serbian republic as it relates to disarming paramilitary formations and individuals by the 11th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: In trying to look at, from the military documents, some of the background to those references to disarming, I wanted to try and see if there was some kind of chain or documentary chain that would help in understanding those references. And I would argue that you can show a documentary chain emanating from the republic level through to the Autonomous Region of Krajina to the municipalities in relation to this issue of deadlines. That resulted in military action on the ground. And I believe this document to be of some significance in that chain of events. And I can go through some of those sections just to highlight what I mean by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: The document is from the republic -- republican Secretariat for National Defence at the Autonomous Region of Krajina and in particular the secretary for the regional Secretariat for National Defence, Colonel Miodrag Sajic. I highlight the very first line which is: "Pursuant to decision number 1/92 of the 16th of April of the Ministry of National Defence of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina," which is the document that we referred to earlier on, the Bogdan Subotic instruction, calling an imminent threat of war and the mobilisation of the TO. If you remember, in that reference, he also said territorial defence or defence should be established at republic, regional and municipal level. And although I'm not 100 per cent sure here, this may well be why Colonel Sajic is in this position as the regional Secretariat for National Defence, in essence a regional Defence body has been established, potentially based on the Subotic instruction of the 16th of April but the document references the Subotic instruction and it calls for a general public mobilisation on the entire territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and makes reference to conscripts being put at the disposal of municipal TO headquarters. It establishes a curfew and in part 5 in particular: "All paramilitary formations and individuals in possession of illegal weapons and ammunition are asked to surrender these weapons and ammunition immediately or not later than 1500 hours on the 11th of May, 1992, to the municipal Territorial Defence headquarters or the nearest public security station." Once this deadline has expired, the responsible bodies shall carry out the search and confiscation of weapons and ammunition and shall apply the most appropriate sanctions. Now, I believe some of the decisions in there link back to that authority or the reference in the Subotic instruction which talked about taking all necessary measures required in the territory. And I would argue here that at the regional level, all necessary measures they have interpreted as establishing a curfew, issuance of deadlines in essence to control the territory in that manner. In the explanation, point 1 and the second bullet of point 2, are references or very close references to the Subotic instruction. So we have the 15th of August mobilisation of the TO and declaration of an imminent threat of war from the republic level. That then passed on by Bogdan Subotic on the 15th of April through his instruction and on the 4th of May at the regional level we have the regional Secretariat for National Defence component of the regional government referencing the Subotic instruction, taking its authority from that instruction, and imposing a curfew and deadlines and mobilisation on the territory of the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. And just I think you may have misspoke. You talked about the 15th of August mobilisation before the 16th of April Subotic order. You were talking about the 15th of April, were you not?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just for the record, the Subotic order which has just been spoken of and the answer is P153. That's the document we looked at earlier. Now, just as an illustration of what you've been telling us, if we could look at the document you cite in footnote 451, that's in a much later section of your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is P717, Your Honours, that may be a different ERN number again of the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So in the list, in the spreadsheet that you gave us under footnote 451, the document which was disclosed under 4.794 does not have an exhibit number. So you're telling us that the exhibit number is P717?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. I apologise that wasn't on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Just to make it clear. No need to apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The title was cited in footnote 451 as, Bosanski Novi Public Security Station Report, dated 15th of August, 1992. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sorry, do you think that's what P717 is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, Mr. Nicholls, if you look at footnote 457, 457, and also 461, we are purportedly dealing also with Exhibit P717. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: What I have for P717, Your Honour, is a security services centre Banja Luka decision about collection centres and prisoners and things of that nature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The three ERN numbers do not tally. In other words, if we are really talking of Exhibit P717, then according to the spreadsheet, the ERN numbers shown under footnote 451, under footnote 457, and under footnote 461, certainly do not tally. So I don't know. I mean, if you can enlighten us on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is I think because some of the ERNs cited in the report may not match ones which have previously been exhibited. I'll have to check this and perhaps come back to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So let's skip this and go straight to the next point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: According to the footnote 451, this is a Bosanski Novi public security station report. According to footnote 457, it's a Sanski Most SJB report. And according to 461, it's a report forwarded by Banja Luka security services, dated 18 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I need to check that, Your Honour. I believe that there are several of these municipality reports contained in a larger document, which is why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It could well be that they are incorporated in the Banja Luka security services report dated 18th August, but I don't know. But certainly you can't have all these documents bearing the same exhibit number when the ERN numbers do not tally.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm told P717 was a set of reports including these different municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Could be, all right. Anyway, you check on that and you'll come back to us either later on today or tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's right, I'm looking at it. It's 32 pages long and it talks about several different municipalities submitted by -- actually comes from Banja Luka security services centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thought it would come from there. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, maybe we can look at this Bosanski Novi portion of the document. If we need to, I can assign that a specific exhibit number but this is within then 717, which is why there was some confusion.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Would you like me to enlighten slightly?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The document is also Defence Exhibit 113. It's also admitted by us at one point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think Mr. Brown can help us with this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think for what it's worth I do remember these documents. I think there were three separate municipality reports. They were then sent to CSB Banja Luka, and they compiled their own report based on those three reports. They are not exactly the same, so I would -- slight element of caution that the compiled report that CSB Banja Luka sent was to some degree of a synthesis of these individual documents. And I think the one I'm referencing here is the individual documents that came from Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's clear enough. Thank you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Let's briefly go through this document. For the record, the translation ERN number is 0096-8599. That is the document you have cited in 451, just so that we know which Novi report we are dealing with. Is that what you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly why you included this report, the section of the report, actually, in this area of this topic on disarmament deadlines, this report in the first paragraph refers to the 11th of May, 1500 hour deadline?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: If I can just quickly go back to the Sajic instruction. The last part of the Sajic instruction stated that: "The presidents of the all people's defence councils were responsible for the implementation of this decision and were given the authority to do so." So that would indicate that this instruction from Sajic was passed down to the municipalities for action. And in my Stakic testimony, I believe there is documentation in Prijedor where it is clear that that actually happened. In relation to this Bosanski Novi document, I draw your attention to the very first section, and a few other sections in -- also in the report. It states: "Pursuant to a decision of the Ministry of National Defence of the Serbian republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, number 1/92 of the 16th of April, 1992, on the decision of the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina in association with the Bosanski Novi municipality Territorial Defence headquarters, and with representatives of organs of the government, this public security station drew up a plan for the confiscation of illegally obtained arms, ammunition, mines and explosives from groups and individuals in the area of the municipality of Bosanski Novi. This plan anticipated all activities being completed by the 11th of May, 1992, at 1500 hours. However, these activities did not have the desired effect on the voluntary relinquishment of arms and apart from that, during the night of the 10th of May in the village of Blagaj Rijeka, according to the reports of a military police patrol, an attack was mounted upon it. These events provoked a series of attacks on the areas and villages with majority Muslim populations." The document then goes on to discuss the removal and in essence of Muslim populated villages in the Blagaj Japra area and in other areas in the municipality and the movement out of those people into detention camps set up in the municipality. It also, I believe, highlights very well this relationship between civilian military and police organs in relation to that. But I flagged up in particular that first section because it is a documented piece of evidence that highlights this relationship and link between the 15th and 16th of April or the 16th of April Subotic instruction, the autonomous region, National Defence document of the 4th of May, the weapon deadline issue and the deadline articulated in this report is identical to the Sajic report. And it also highlights that where they say that voluntary relinquishment of weapons did not happen, as well as their being this reference to the attack, that there were these attacks on Muslim villages in the area. So the reference, appropriate sanctions, the appropriate sanctions reference in the 4th of May would seem to be somewhat apparent from this document. I would also refer you back to the comments of Mr. Vjestica at the 16th assembly session, who stated that he was aware of what was going on in his neighbouring municipalities and in fact had visited there. And he himself discussed the issue of deadlines and the surrender of weapons. Some had been handed over and some hadn't. So for me this ties in, this documentary evidence, about the issue of deadlines and the importance placed on this issue and the fact that military attacks and actions against non-Serbs were occurring in relation to those -- those decrees and decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 2.13 of your report, you refer to the 8th of May conclusions of the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff, and in that document, we see that: "The strictest sanctions will be imposed on those who refuse to return weapons, referring" - this is in point 3 - "to the requirement of the presidents of the National Defence councils to report to the war staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina about any actions they may have taken in order to disarm paramilitary units and individuals possessing illegal weapons."

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, this is another decision, this time from the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff prior to this deadline of the 11th of May, reaffirming the issue of the reporting of what action was going to be taken in relation to that. I also draw your attention to point 4 of that decision of the 8th of May which states that at one hour intervals the Banja Luka Radio was to broadcast announcements to citizens to return weapons so that peace can be maintained in the area. So again this is decisions and actions prior to this 11th of May deadline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: May I go back just very briefly to what was finally -- the last document, 00968599? I, in fact, have found it. It is not -- I don't think it's P717. It probably has to have a new exhibit number because it is a separate report. The disclosure number if it helps the Prosecutor is 4.794. And I think before we go any further, it probably ought to be assigned an exhibit number because it really is a different document than P717.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be P2423, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For your information, Mr. Nicholls, and Mr. Ackerman, I have found here on my laptop reference when Ms. Korner introduced this document during one of the reading sessions. And there is a description of what this document is but I can't help you any further beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I was originally believed this document had to be assigned a new number, received some information that it was actually part of another one. I will clear that up if we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay, Mr. Nicholls, let's proceed, let's not waste time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just because we have been interrupted, with this issue, paragraph 2.14 of your report, I think begins to sum up what you've been telling us here - is that correct - that the ARK decisions relating to weapons surrender and the preparations for forceful action is part of a recognised plan passed down to municipal bodies and acted upon and in some areas the decision to disarm the population appeared to have been coordinated across municipal boundaries?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think this is pretty clear, we can do this quite quickly. Footnote 264, this is Exhibit P904, it's a Kljuc municipal Crisis Staff document dated the 9th of May, 1992. And point 2 states: "Read out the order to disarm citizens that you received earlier." You've cited this as an example of that dissemination of the order; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: I would add I think there is other documents that would indicate that and I believe in my Stakic testimony in Prijedor municipality that I also hinted that -- or hinted but made reference it that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, as I said I don't propose to repeat the testimony which Your Honours have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think we have heard enough about -- not heard enough from the witness, heard enough from other witnesses and seen enough of similar documents actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'd like to quickly look at - I think this is important - the document you cite in footnote 269. This is P195. It's a CSB Banja Luka instruction dated the 14th of May, 1992. And it's fairly self-evident but can you tell us why you included this document which relates to the Autonomous Region of Krajina disarmament decisions?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Well, again I think it's directly linked to the decisions taken at the regional level in relation to disarmament and in this case, the police are making concrete plans for obtaining and seizing those weapons in accordance with the decisions that were -- I've already articulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And again, in other documents, in 1st Krajina Corps documents, I believe, you have found references to these weapons deadlines issued by the Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes. The military appeared very aware of the fact that deadlines were appearing and they make reference -- a number of references in this period to specifically to the deadlines and dates, and then as I said later on they make references to their own operations in relation to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Another document I think we have time to quickly go through related to this topic is the one you footnote in 389, this is Exhibit 638. This is a Sanski Most Territorial Defence order issued by Colonel Anicic relating to disarmament operations in Sanski Most and actually in the title characterising the disarmament operation as a combat task. Can you tell us about this document and how it shows coordination in the disarmament process between TO units, VRS units, and police units?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: This order, as you highlight, is entitled disarmament operations in Sanski Most which is revealing in itself. It talks about, in part 2, after the mobilisation of the TO units of Sanski Most municipality we managed to maintain control of the territory and organise the defence of the Serbian-populated areas in the area of the municipality in good time. The task of the TO of Sanski Most municipality is to disarm enemy forces in the territory of the municipality by engaging the wartime units of the TO staff. It later on goes on, and to maintain in coordinated action with units of the 6th Brigade which was a brigade of General Talic's command, complete control of the territory in order to ensure stable functioning of our government and create conditions for unobstructed life and work. The order then discusses a coordinated military operation with the Territorial Defence and the 6th Brigade which they articulate as being a disarmament operation. It makes mention of artillery preparations to disarm settlements of Mahala, Otoka, Muhici and others, in coordination with the 6th Brigade. It gives instructions to its own mortar unit of that TO to take up positions in order to carry out artillery preparations and to attack by firing at significant targets in a number of villages, highlighted in paragraph 8. And it gives tasks to the various components of the Territorial Defence. It makes mention in paragraph 15, upon the completion of the task take prisoners of war to the sports hall, the secondary school and hand over war booty to the Sanski Most Serbian TO staff. This would -- I would imagine require some element of coordination to have that facility available and made available. And it highlights on paragraph 16, readiness for the attack at 0500 hours on the 26th of May. So I think this is a very obvious order to the Territorial Defence for a combined operation to carry out disarmament that will involve artillery preparation, artillery shelling and they anticipate that prisoners of war, a requirement to take them to the facility annotated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if you look at page -- paragraph 218 of your report, we don't need to go through the entire paragraph or read it, but this document we've just gone through is an example of the process of disarmament you refer to in that section, is it not?

utterances.speaker: EWAN BROWN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have about two minutes, I guess. I think maybe if we break now, I don't think I can get through the next section.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Mr. Brown, we'll be stopping here. We'll continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I just ask Your Honour when we are finishing tomorrow? I remember hearing it may be a little early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to finish a bit early. I still have to contact the President's office to tell me exactly what time I need to leave but it will be definitely 12.00 or before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.
